unit_name: Sixth Panzer Army (Sixth SS Panzer Army)
source_locator: R434: p. 394; R175: table of 1944, 10 November row
current_activity: The Sixth Panzer Army is ordered to mass near Cologne and is to move into the OB West theater on 7 November
notes: Event date: CMH Siegfried Line Campaign ch. 17 p. 394: "When the Sixth Panzer Army, for example, earmarked for the counteroffensive, was ordered to mass near Cologne"; the OB WEST war diary entry: "the Commander-in-Chief WEST will order the transfer of Sixth Panzer Army to the OB WEST theater on 7 November"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 6. Panzerarmee, table 1944: 10 November, OB West, "Westen". Event definition: the transfer ordered for 7 November; the Lexikon row is dated 10 November. Event support: two source families: CMH (quoting the OB WEST war diary) for the day and place; the Lexikon table for OB West. Location: Cologne with a precision of 25 km, the massing area named by CMH. Location approximate: a representative point for the massing area near Cologne. Location support: CMH names the area near Cologne. Commander: Oberstgruppenführer Josef Dietrich. Context: The headquarters is the one the Germans kept out of the line for the Ardennes counteroffensive.

unit_name: Sixth Panzer Army (Sixth SS Panzer Army)
source_locator: R644: p. 76-77; R643: listing under the 6th Panzer Army heading; R175: table of 1944, December row
current_activity: The Sixth Panzer Army opens the main effort of Wacht am Rhein on the front from Monschau to Krewinkel
notes: Event date: CMH Ardennes ch. 5 p. 76: "Monschau to Krewinkel, was narrower than that of its southern partner"; p. 77: "the Sixth Panzer did have a timetable: one day for penetration and breakout, one day to get the armor over the Hohes Venn"; Nafziger 944GLAA (15 December 1944): "6th Panzer Army: Oberstgruppenführer der Waffen-SS J.Dietrich" under "OB West: Feldmarschal G. von Runstedt" and "Army Group B Feldmarschal W. Model"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 6. Panzerarmee, table 1944: December, Heeresgruppe B, "Westen". Event definition: the opening of the offensive on 16 December. Event support: three source families: CMH for the day and the front, Nafziger for the army group, Lexikon for the month. Location: Hollerath with a precision of 25 km, a point near the middle of the Monschau-Krewinkel front. Location approximate: a representative point for the middle of the front. Location support: CMH names the ends of the front and the NAF file lists the army under Army Group B. Commander: Oberstgruppenführer Josef Dietrich. Opponents: US V Corps (99th and 2nd Infantry Divisions) and VIII Corps (14th Cavalry Group).

unit_name: Sixth Panzer Army (Sixth SS Panzer Army)
location_qualifier: area near St. Vith where the army was assembling; headquarters place not named
source_locator: R515: p. 51; R537: p. 140; R175: Einsatz, Gliederung, 21 January 1945
current_activity: Hitler orders the Sixth Panzer Army out of the Ardennes on 22 January to move east against the Russian offensive
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 2 p. 51: "On that day Hitler ordered the Sixth Panzer Army to quit the Ardennes entirely and to transfer with all speed to the east"; CMH The Last Offensive ch. 8 p. 140: "Hitler on 22 January, when ordering the Sixth Panzer Army to the east". Event definition: the order of 22 January in CMH; the Lexikon table gives 21 January for the army in Hungary under the Replacement Army/OKH and its text gives the end of January. Event support: two source families (CMH for the day; the Lexikon, Tessin, for the move to Hungary). Location: Saint-Vith with a precision of 25 km, the area near St. Vith where CMH p. 32 says the army headquarters and SS corps were to assemble; the headquarters place is not named. Location approximate: the area near St. Vith for the army. Location support: CMH p. 32 places the army headquarters in the rear near St. Vith. Commander: Generaloberst der Waffen-SS Josef Dietrich. Opponents: US First Army. Context: The army headquarters, two SS panzer corps, four SS panzer divisions and the Führer Begleit and Führer Grenadier Brigades went east. The existing relation to Army Group B (CR0687) stays open because no source read gives the date the army left that army group.
